transcript.answer: No, not any more. ADR-039 originally decided that the org-default review agent should be pinned to a different model family from the implementer. The settings UI would also warn when both resolved to the same family. An amendment dated 2026-10-14 reversed this. `code-review` and `code-review-recheck` now run on `gemini-4-argon`, the same family as the implementation loop's `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`. `code-review-reply` stays on `claude-sonnet-4-6`. The amendment says cross-family review "is no longer a rule, only one input to the model choice." The reason given is a local bench on five merged PRs, where Argon found all five that finished, against four of six for Sonnet. The amendment says that catch rate outweighed the self-preference risk. The cost is that Argon is about 3x slower and about 40% dearer. I read only the truncated excerpts, not the full ADR, so there may be further detail I missed.
